chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us via this chain, from al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abu Ishaq, this matter has been delayed twice.'

key_terms.الْأَمْر: The matter (referring to the Imamate or the rise of the Qa'im)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the delay of the Mahdi's rise?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) informs Ishaq ibn Ammar that the 'matter' (referring to the rise of the Mahdi or the Imamate) has been postponed twice, indicating a history of delays in the fulfillment of divine promise regarding the Qa'im. This narration is central to the Shia doctrine of *al-Ghayba al-Kubra* (the Major Occultation), illustrating that the delay is not an absence but a divinely ordained period of preparation and testing for the faithful. The 'two postponements' are often interpreted by scholars as referring to the transition from the Minor to the Major Occultation or specific historical intervals of concealment before the final reappearance.
